To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

low-grade germinal-matrix intraventricular hemorrahage (GM- IVH) in extremely low gestational-age neonates (ELGA) was associated with significantly reduced cerebral blood flow and cerebral oxygen metabolism.

extremely low gestational aged neonates with low grade germinal matrix-intraparenchymal hemorrhage have consistently lower cerebral blood flow and cerebral oxygen metabolism than extremely preterm infants without hemorrhages.
extremely preterm infants with low-grade germian matrix intraventricular (GM-IV) hemorrhage have reduced cerebral blood flow and cerebral oxygen metabolism, but normal cerebral oxygen saturation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel noninvasive optical techniques for monitoring cerebral hemodynamics and oxygen metabolism in the neonatal brain.
the development of a non-invasive bedside technique to assess cerebral blood flow, oxygenation and metabolism in premature infants at risk of developing brain damage.
the long-term impact on brain function of the most common complication of extremely preterm birth: low grade germinal matrix intraventricular haemorrhage.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of FD-NIRS and DC-S in the NICU is a promising tool for monitoring brain development, especially in preterm infants.
low-grade GM- IVH in ELGA neonate is associated with a long-term reduction in cerebral blood flow and cerebral oxygen metabolism, which may be associated with long-term neurodevelopmental impairment.
reduced cerebral blood flow and reduced cerebral oxygen metabolism in extremely premature neonate with low-grade GM IVH may be an indicator of long-term neurologic damage.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the combination of FDNIRS- and DCS-based measurements of cerebral oxygen metabolism may have clinical benefit in monitoring the evolution of low-grade GM-IHV in ELGA neonate and potentially predicting long-term neurodevelopmental outcome.
GM-IVH in ELGA neonate is associated with reduced CBFi and cerebral oxygen metabolism (i.e., CMRO2i), and that these changes persist even after resolution of the hemorrhages.
the use of FDNIRS- DCS methods may have a potential clinical benefit for monitoring and evaluating the effects of low-grade GM -IVH on the premature brain.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of FDNIRS- DCS methods can be used for monitoring the evolution and response of GM-IVh in extremely preterm infants.

the combination of FD-NIRS-DCS can be used to measure CBFi and an index of CMRO2i at the bedside in ELGA infants with low-grade GMIVH, and these measures may have better sensitivity to the effects of the hemorrhage compared to SO2.
the combination of FDNIRS- DCS methods can detect subtle changes in cerebral oxygenation and metabolism that are not detected by conventional monitoring.
